title.narrative: Farmtrack Consulting Limited and University of the West of Scotland

description.narrative: To develop a novel and environmentally friendly female fruit fly protein baited trap using locally available raw materials; to enhance supply chains (mangoes); and to address a key global food production challenge and contribute towards both societal and economic impact within Kenya and Africa.

To develop a novel and environmentally friendly female fruit fly protein baited trap using locally available raw materials; to enhance supply chains (mangoes); and to address a key global food production challenge and contribute towards both societal and economic impact within Kenya and Africa. Innovation area – Pest control It is anticipated that 3 new full-time jobs and 20 casual jobs will be delivered from this project. In addition, 16 new jobs will be delivered within 5 years post KTP. Seven employees of the company will develop new skills in areas including: supply chain management, logistics, downstream production & product commercialisation, adding to streamlined operations and systems. ODA – In Kenya, rural poverty is estimated at 38.8% (World Bank: Kenya Economic Update 2018). Studies suggest that use of traps in place of synthetic pesticides reduces household expenditure by 46.3%.The use of traps can increase rural household income by 22.4%-48%. The technology will enable farmers to produce higher volumes of marketable fruits, generate higher prices, contribute to nutritional security, and reduce insecticide expenditure. The new product, due to its high effectiveness/low labour costs, and 30% of the extra income being ploughed back into production, will add to fruit production sustainability and higher yields. The product will be developed from a natural corn based proteins by-product. Since corn is a major staple food crop in Kenya this will not exert pressure on production systems to provide raw materials, thereby reducing carbon emissions. (Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS) Economic Survey 2019). There will be no runoff into water systems, no accumulation of pesticides in the food chain, and no environmental contamination. Current crop losses due to fruit flies can be up to 100% without interventions. The novel technology will reduce this wastage by 80% in the first three years after adoption and add 10% disposable income to farmers. Invasion of fruits in Kenya by fruit flies has caused the production of low-grade fruits leading to banning of export to European Union countries and the USA. Smallholder farmers the majority of whom live below the poverty line produce mango. Losses due to the fruit fly can be as high as 100%. The development of a sustainably managed product will result in production of high grade fruits and higher prices in export markets thereby improving the livelihoods of poor farmers.
